transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well… I guess I’m here because I just don’t have the push I used to. I used to go to choir, do my quilting, visit folks… but lately most days I just sit at home with the TV on low. I know people are expecting me sometimes, but I still don’t get myself up to go.
About how long have you been feeling this way—weeks, months, or longer?
It’s been longer than weeks. I’d say it’s been building since I retired from the school office… a little over two years ago now.
Over these past two years, have you also been feeling sad, down, or empty most days, or is it mainly that you lack the energy or motivation to do things?

It’s mainly the lack of push, I’d say. I’m not sitting there crying all day or anything like that. I just… don’t get myself going like I used to. Choir, quilting, visiting people — I know I ought to go, and folks may be expecting me, but most days I just stay home with the TV on low.
Have you or anyone close to you noticed any changes in your memory, concentration, or ability to think clearly over these past two years?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything big like that. I mean, I might forget little things now and then, but I don’t know that it’s changed much. My thinking feels about the same to me.
Have you noticed any other physical changes over these two years, like gaining weight, feeling unusually cold, or having dry skin or hair changes?
No, not that I’ve noticed. My weight seems about the same, and I don’t think I’ve been colder than usual. I haven’t paid much attention to my skin or hair, but nothing stands out to me.
Have you ever had a stroke, head injury, or been diagnosed with any other neurological or medical condition around the time these changes started?
No, not that I know of. I haven’t had a stroke or a head injury, and I don’t recall any doctor telling me I had some other condition around then.
When you do occasionally go to choir or quilting, or watch something on TV, do you still find yourself enjoying it, or does it feel flat either way?

It’s more… flat, I guess. I don’t have the push I used to have to go to choir or quilting, or even go visit folks. If I do watch TV, it’s usually just on low and I’m sitting there, not really enjoying it much, even when I know people are expecting me somewhere.
Have you had any trouble keeping up with things like paying bills, managing your medications, or handling other daily tasks the way you used to?

Some things, yes. I don’t keep up like I used to. I’ve had to step back from leading choir and helping with projects at the senior center because I’d say I would do something and then not get it done. My church friends check on me more now than they used to.
Have you or anyone close to you noticed you repeating the same questions or stories, or having trouble learning new information or finding your way in familiar places?

I don’t think so. I mean, nobody’s told me I keep asking the same things, and I don’t think I’ve been getting lost in places I know. Learning new things… I’m not sure, I just haven’t really been doing much new lately.

When you don't finish things like paying bills or choir projects, is it because you get confused or lose track of the steps involved, or is it more that you just don't feel motivated to start or continue?

It’s more that I just don’t feel the push to start, or to keep going. I don’t think I’m getting mixed up on the steps so much. I just end up sitting at home, with the TV on low, even when I know I ought to be at choir or quilting or visiting somebody.
Over these past two years, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, like trouble falling asleep, waking up early, or sleeping much more than you used to?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a big change with my sleep one way or the other. Some nights are better than others, but I can’t say it’s been much different.
Over these past two years, have you had any feelings of guilt, worthlessness, or hopelessness about yourself or your life?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve been feeling guilty or worthless in a big way. Sometimes I get down on myself because I’m not doing as much, but I wouldn’t say hopeless, no.
Are you currently being treated for any other medical conditions, or taking any regular medications, that started around the time these changes began two years ago?
I’m not sure. I don’t think there was any new medical problem or medicine that started right around then. Nothing I can think of, anyway.
When you don't make it to choir or quilting, do you feel indifferent about missing it, or do you still wish you could go but just can't get yourself motivated?

I still wish I could go, I guess. It’s not that I don’t care about choir or quilting anymore. I just don’t have the push like I used to. Most days I end up sitting at home with the TV on low, even when I know people are expecting me.

When something upsetting or sad happens—like bad news about a friend or a family issue—do you still feel affected by it, or does it seem like your emotional reactions in general, good or bad, have become more flat and muted?

I still feel sad if something bad happens, I think. It’s more that I just don’t have the push I used to. Choir, quilting, visiting people… I know folks expect me, and I still end up sitting at home with the TV on low. It’s not so much that I don’t feel anything.
Have you or anyone close to you noticed any changes in how you move—like your walking becoming slower, your hands feeling stiff, or any shaking or tremor—over these past two years?

No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed any shaking or my hands being stiff. I move maybe a little slower just because I’m getting older, but nothing that really changed all of a sudden or that anyone’s pointed out to me.
Do you have any history of high blood pressure, diabetes, or high cholesterol that a doctor has told you about?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember a doctor telling me I have any of those, but I may not be remembering everything right.
Over these two years, have you noticed any change in how well you keep up with your own personal care—like bathing, dressing, or eating regularly?

I bathe and dress myself, and I do eat, but I don’t keep up with things like I used to. I’ve had to step back from leading choir and helping with projects at the senior center because I don’t follow through on what I said I’d do. And church friends check on me more now, just to make sure I’m all right.
I’m not sure what you mean exactly. I don’t think I’ve noticed anything else to say about that.
Does anyone in your immediate family—parents or siblings—have a history of dementia, Parkinson's disease, or other memory-related illnesses?
I’m not sure. I don’t really know of anyone in my close family being told they had dementia or Parkinson’s, but I can’t say for certain.
